featured_reviews.review_text: They are trying to cheat customers. I asked for a full tank but the attendant stopped at 100 (I know he heard me correctly because he stopped at 100 manually, rather than the pump stopping on its own). featured_reviews.review_text:
Asked petrol filling person to fill for 930(Nau sau tees) but he filled for 230(Do sau tees). Then I asked him to fill for 700₹ more. Then he took the 230 counter to 700 without resetting and was chatting with me on some random credit card for saving money on fuel payment. I was unaware of this since was making UPI payment. For 930₹ he filled only 700₹ petrol.

After 4-5 days my bike tank went into reserve earlier than expected. I went to this pump and met the manager and complained about this. He asked me to speak to that specific person. The fuel filler guy came and said there was a higher amount of 230₹ in his hisab that day due to this and then filled my bike with 230₹ petrol.

Shameful act. Had I not gone there and met the manager who seemed helpful, the fuel filler guy would have easily made 230₹. God knows how many customers are cheated like this everyday.

featured_reviews.review_text:
NAZAR HATI DURGATNA GHATI
I told them to fill petrol worth 500. While they were filling, another guy came with a QR code and asked me to make the payment, clearly to distract me. I questioned him, “Kitne ka bhara?”
He confidently replied, “kitna bola tumhne utna hi bhara”
Soon, two more guys came and backed him up, insisting they had filled 500.
I asked again, this time more firmly, how much he had actually filled. Finally, he admitted he had filled only 400 and started making excuses, saying he misheard and thought I said 400. He returned 100 in cash.
All of them were involved. That’s how the owner affords expensive SUVs

🚨 Beware of Cheating at this Petrol Pump! 🚨

I had a very bad experience here with DEF fluid filling. First of all, when I asked one person if DEF was available, he confidently said “No”. Then another person came and said “Yes” – clearly trying to confuse customers.

I purchased 10 liters DEF for ₹850. My car’s DEF tank capacity is 20 liters, and it was already at 54% (Approximately 10 litres). So, after adding 10 liters, it should have reached 100% full.

But after they “filled” it, the meter showed only 71%. That means they filled just 4 liters instead of 10 liters. When I questioned them, they gave silly excuses like “The remaining fluid in the can won’t come out”. They also did not even use a proper funnel – just pushed a pipe inside carelessly.

When I checked the can, more than 5 liters were still left inside, but the staff shamelessly claimed it was “finished”. I’ve also added pictures of Car DEF level and remaining volume of DEF in Can. This is nothing but open cheating and fraud with customers.

1)  They charge for 10 liters but fill less.
2)  Staff keep confusing answers to trap customers.
3)  No proper equipment or honesty in service.

⚠️ My advice: Avoid this petrol pump at all costs. They are looting people in the name of DEF fluid. Please always come out of your vehicle and check carefully while refueling here. This pump cannot be trusted.

•	Vehicle No.: MH47BE0360

I had a very concerning experience at Anuradha Gas Station (Indian Oil), JVLR Andheri East.

On 15 June 2026, I filled petrol and the staff initially told me the bill amount was around ₹3,491. I was surprised because I had observed the meter and expected the amount to be around ₹2,700. After questioning them, they produced a bill showing ₹3,391, and I ended up paying the amount through UPI.

Later, when I reached home and checked the receipt carefully, I noticed that the receipt time was 20:41, whereas my UPI payment was made at 21:13. This clearly indicated that the receipt did not belong to my transaction. I immediately returned to the petrol pump, and after discussion, the staff admitted it was a "mistake" and refunded the excess amount.

What makes this even more suspicious is that during a previous visit, I witnessed another customer arguing that petrol had not been filled into his vehicle despite being charged.

Such incidents raise serious concerns about transparency and customer trust. Customers should carefully verify the meter reading, receipt details, and transaction amount before making payment. The management and authorities should investigate these repeated complaints and take strict action if any fraudulent practices are found.

I usually prefer filling petrol at Indian Oil petrol pumps, but yesterday I had a rather disappointing experience. While returning home, I stopped at this petrol station to fill fuel in my car.

We had asked for petrol worth ₹1005, but when I looked carefully, the meter had already shown two lines before the filling even started. He then claimed the machine had auto-cut at ₹840 and returned the remaining amount because I had already paid ₹1005 in advance. Even while returning the balance, the amount was ₹5 short.

What felt even stranger was that once we started driving, the fuel indicator in the car barely moved up. Only God knows what actually happened.

Overall, the entire experience left me feeling cheated and deeply disappointed. It is sad how, at times, people compromise their honesty and integrity for such small gains. Trust is something customers carry with them when they stop at a fuel station, and once broken, it leaves a very unpleasant feeling behind.

Ironically, my name is also Anuradha, and coincidentally, the gas station was called “Anuradha Gas Station.”

IndianOil supplies fuels strictly in accordance with IS 17021:2018 specifications and all applicable quality standards.
